faqs.q: Is Dirty Flamenco traditional flamenco or Spanish guitar?
faqs.a: Traditional flamenco. The repertoire is palos, the traditional forms: bulerias, solea, alegrias and tangos. A Spanish guitar booking plays familiar songs with a Spanish flavor; a flamenco booking plays the forms themselves. Dirty Flamenco is fronted by Gary Meyers and booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

Under dinner it plays at the level of the conversation, so the table talks across it. The set piece is louder on purpose, because it's the part everyone stops to watch. The trio sets the level to the space and the crowd, and if your venue has a sound limit, give us the number and it plays under it.

faqs.q: Is Spanish guitar right for a wedding ceremony?
faqs.a: Yes. Nylon strings carry a processional and a recessional without amplification in most spaces, and the repertoire moves between Spanish pieces and the songs a couple asks for.
Yes. With a dancer the trio becomes a quartet, and the dancer is the set piece. Whether an evening wants one depends on whether the program has space for a set piece in it.
